Subject: Request: pen test report and confirmation of retest policy

Hi Rachel,

We’re preparing Acme’s vendor security review for Q2 and have a couple of questions about Redwood’s penetration testing program. Can you please confirm the following:

- Do you have a recent full pen test report that covers internet-facing services and internal auth flows? If so, what is the report date?
- Our procurement policy typically requires a report within the last 12 months. Is Redwood able to provide evidence that would be accepted if the report date is outside that window?
- If remediation is required, do you support an evidence-only retest (verification of fixes) or do you always require a full re-test?
- Who is the testing firm you use and can you provide firm credentials / scope / methodology (e.g., authenticated tests, OWASP adherence)?

We appreciate a short answer and any supporting artifacts or links. If easier, we can schedule a quick 20-min call.

Thanks,
Aisha Gomez
Senior Security Analyst
Acme Software

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the clear list — happy to confirm details below and attach the summary artifacts you asked for. Short answers first, then a bit more context.

- Recent report: We performed a full external + authenticated pen test (internet-facing + selected internal admin paths) in October 2025. Summary report: redwood-pen-test-20251015-summary.pdf (attached).
- Report age / acceptance: Our standard position is that a full report is considered current for 12 months from the report date. For customers with procurement requirements that insist on <=12 months, we offer a targeted verification engagement (remediation verification) or a retest window to meet your timeline. We can also provide the testing firm’s workpapers under NDA.
- Retest types: We support two common paths: (1) targeted verification (also called remediation validation) where the tester validates specific fixes and issue closures — this is typically accepted by auditors for remediation evidence; or (2) full re-test which repeats the engagement scope. Which is required depends on your audit tolerance and the age of the vulnerabilities.
- Testing firm & methodology: The engagement was performed by SecureEdge Labs (CREST-aligned testing team). Methodology: authenticated + external scan, OWASP Top 10 and API layer checks, privilege escalation attempts, and sampling of internal admin flows. We follow a risk-based sampling approach and provide workpapers for substantive findings.

Attachments: redwood-pen-test-20251015-summary.pdf, remediation-worksheet-20260329.xlsx (worksheet lists open/closed items and suggested verification steps).

If you’d like, I can loop in our vendor lead and our remediation owner to discuss retest timing/pricing. We typically provision a remediation verification slot within 2–4 weeks depending on vendor availability.

Best,

Rachel Kim
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Also — can you confirm estimated retest fees or whether this is included under certain contractual support tiers?

Hi Aisha,

Appreciate the detailed read — answers inline below.

- Scope enumeration: The pen test scope included all public endpoints under api.redwood.ai and the management console at console.redwood.ai (management API endpoints that are documented in our internal API spec). I’ve redacted hostnames in the attached worksheet for sharing; if you need a fuller mapping we can provide a scoped list under an NDA.

- Verification approach: SecureEdge supports both modes. For most customers, a remediation verification engagement consists of targeted validation (live checks against fixed issues) plus reviewer attestations. SecureEdge will perform exploit attempts only if the fix requires it — otherwise they document validation steps and the evidence captured. That approach is generally accepted by customer auditors when accompanied by the tester’s statement and workpapers.

- Redacted workpapers: Yes — we can provide redacted workpapers that remove internal IP and operational details. Those are provided under our standard evidence-sharing NDA.

- Fees / contractual coverage: Retest fees are not included in our standard free tier. For customers on an enterprise contract (Dedicated or Private), we include one remediation verification within a 12-month window as part of the security support addendum. For other customers, SecureEdge charges a targeted verification fee — typical ballpark is $6–10k depending on scope. We can confirm exact pricing after we review your required endpoints.

Next steps I propose:
1) If Acme can mark the items you want validated on the remediation-worksheet-20260329.xlsx, we’ll share a redacted scope and request NDA if you want workpapers.
2) We’ll request availability from SecureEdge and propose a 2–4 week verification window.
3) If Acme requires a full re-test instead of verification, we’ll provide an updated estimate and timeline.

I’ll also loop in our remediation operations lead (Priyom) to book vendor availability — Priyom, can you confirm typical lead time from SecureEdge and whether we have any discounted slots for enterprise customers?

Best,
Rachel
